node.title: Re: Killer byte tripping up Perl?
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
If you're reading binary data, you should always [doc://binmode] the filehandle, or use the three-argument open and specify the :raw layer. Don't use a plain [doc://print] to show the data, use [mod://Data::Dump] or [doc://Data::Dumper] with $Data::Dumper::Useqq=1;. Plus, note that your while () is still going to split the input on [doc://$/] (if you haven't set it to anything else), so you might want to look into [doc://read] to read fixed-size chunks of data ([doc://$/] has a special mode for that, but I like [doc://read] better).

Update: I see [haj] and [Laurent_R] have made similar points too. In particular, don't [doc://chomp] binary data!

Another note: I wrote about "safer" piped opens [id://1180578|here].
